summary: API-key security chain + EventsController are well-structured, follow existing project patterns (WebhookSecretVerifier hash discipline, SubscriberServiceImpl rate-limit idiom, AppException/GlobalErrorHandler mapping). Response-code matrix, uniform 401, project-scoped resolution, error-isolation all implemented correctly. No critical/major issues.

findings.finding: The controller wraps dispatch in try/catch(Throwable) even though FunnelEventService.dispatchForSubscriber is itself error-isolated and never throws. The extra catch is redundant belt-and-braces.
findings.reason: Intentional defense-in-depth per Decision 12 (endpoint must NEVER 5xx); cheap and documented. Keeping it guards against a future change to the dispatcher's contract.

findings.finding: Logs carry projectId/subscriberId/error-class only — no event_name, no key material, no PII. Matches Decision 16 PII rule.
findings.reason: Good practice confirmed, not a defect.

findings.finding: Verified dispatchForSubscriber(projectId, subscriberId, TRIGGER_EVENT, eventName, 0) matches FunnelEventService signature; findById(projectId,id) and findByTelegramUserId(projectId,uid) match SubscriberService; AppException factories map to 429/404/401; @Valid maps to 400 via GlobalErrorHandler.
findings.reason: All call sites verified against definitions.

findings.finding: Filter is deliberately NOT a @Component (would auto-register globally and 401 every request); instantiated inside the integrations SecurityFilterChain. Documented in class javadoc + the bean method.
findings.reason: Correct fix for the global-filter-registration pitfall; caught and resolved during implementation.
